digest.component_or_area: verifier model-class resolution across plan-review, completion, and code-review gates
propositions: Three verifier code paths select the model by comparing cfg.model to the default constant, so any non-default (e.g. Bedrock) model reads as an operator choice and the downgrade silently stops applying.
The fix replaces the equality tests with a single reserved-class resolution via resolve_model_string, which resolves trivial/standard/frontier and returns any other string unchanged.

The code-review.yaml verify step declares no model: key and config.resolve_model returns step-or-workflow-or-cfg.model without calling resolve_model_string, so Pass-2 verify still runs on the frontier model and the class is never resolved.
resolve_class emits a provider-qualified id, so with no class configured the verifier model string changes from bare to provider-qualified form, breaking the promised byte-identical back-compat.

_verifier_cfg has real callers at xcheck.py:198 and xcheck.py:336 that must be tested through those callers, since isolated tests can pass while a caller passing plain cfg leaves Pass-2/Pass-4 on the frontier model.
A cross-provider negative control is required so that with classes configured for a non-default provider, no verifier path resolves a model belonging to a different provider.
